messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.example>
To: Kate Johnson <kate.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: GDPR, DPA & SCC next steps (ACME Health)

Hi Kate —

Thanks again for the time on the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the compliance items you raised: 

1) Roles: You confirmed ACME Health will act as the data controller and Redwood will be the data processor for the hosted inference integration. Please let me know if that understanding changes.

2) DPA request: You asked for our standard DPA to review and sign. I can start that process — attaching our most recent DPA (v2) in my follow-up to legal.

3) SCCs: For cross-border transfers from the EU, we discussed using the EU Standard Contractual Clauses. Based on controller→processor flow, Module 2 is the appropriate module to include; I will confirm with legal.

4) SOC 2 / HIPAA: You asked about SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA posture. Quick update: our SOC 2 Type II audit is in progress and we expect a report by Q3 2026. We currently support HIPAA controls via BAA options in private deployments — we can escalate to the solutions team if ACME needs formal HIPAA confirmation for hosted endpoints.

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll loop in legal (Laura) and engineering (Dev) to prepare the DPA and SCC Module 2 template; target to get materials to you within 48 hours.
- Can you confirm the legal contact who will sign the DPA (name & email) and whether you need any additional technical documentation (SOC2 interim evidence, encryption/KMS details)?

Happy to hop on a quick call with legal if helpful — otherwise I’ll send the DPA + SCC draft for review.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.co@redwood.example
(415) 555-0173

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary — this looks right from our side. A few clarifications: 

• Controller/Processor: Confirmed — ACME Health is the controller for patient data and Redwood would be the processor for the inference service.
• DPA: Please send your DPA for review. Our legal team prefers to review the vendor DPA first before proffering changes. Our signing contact is: Kate Johnson (kate.johnson@acmehealth.com) and I will loop in our Contracts lead at legal@acmehealth.com.
• SCCs: We do require SCCs for EU→US transfers. Module for controller→processor is what we expect — if you can include the processor-oriented SCC module we can review.
• SOC 2 / HIPAA: We noted your SOC 2 timeline on the call; our security team will want interim evidence if the Type II report is not yet final. We would also like confirmation of encryption in transit at a minimum.

If you can get the DPA + SCC template over today / tomorrow that will help accelerate our procurement review.

Thanks,
Kate
Director, IT & Security | ACME Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>

Marissa —

Thanks for the ping. Attached are two items to start the review: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf (our current DPA baseline) and SCC_Module_2_template.pdf (SCC language appropriate for controller→processor transfers). Highlights / proposed approach below: 

- Roles: We will document ACME as controller and Redwood as processor in section 2 of the DPA.
- SCC module: Module 2 (controller→processor) is the correct module for the relationship described. I’ve included the processor-oriented SCC clauses in the SCC_Module_2_template.pdf so the ACME legal team can review.
- SOC 2 / interim evidence: Because our Type II report is not final until Q3 2026, we can provide interim evidence: a summary of scope, control mapping, and SOC 2 bridge letter. I will prepare a short evidence pack (1–2 pages) for ACME security.
- Encryption / technical notes (Dev please confirm): we will represent encryption in transit via TLS 1.2+ by default; for hosted customers keys are managed by Redwood KMS; for private deployments we support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS). Dev — please confirm exact TLS versions supported and any additional notes about ciphers or mTLS capabilities.

Next steps: 
1) Marissa — send the attached DPA + SCC draft to Kate and legal@acmehealth.com.
2) ACME reviews and redlines; we take counter-redlines.
3) Once terms agreed, we push DPA/SCC to DocuSign (I can prepare the envelope).

I’m cc’ing Dev above for the technical confirmation — once we have Dev’s lines we should be able to meet ACME’s request within 48 hours.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
